name: jstack
description: Agent workflow skills: get battle-ready on a topic (load every relevant skill, survey recent changes, read core files), hand off sessions, split off a verbatim copy of the session into a new terminal, audit completed work trust-nothing (a subagent reviews from source and reports a triaged verdict back to the session, or a fresh terminal you drive), reverify a whole day's shipped work across every repo against the timeline, show the result of the current topic in its real viewer, commit + push session work, install bundled rules. The timeline is the single running memory: bin/log_event writes a sqlite store (agent/submode/session-tagged entries with direct/indirect origin; the store is the only artifact) and serves seat queries via `log_event tail`. PreToolUse hook injects path-matched rules at edit time regardless of launch CWD. bin/pict (prompt injection checking tool) renders everything a session spawned from a given directory would receive — globals, CLAUDE.md walk-up, auto-memory, timeline injection, anchored path rules, hook injectors — as one ordered markdown document with per-source token weights. SessionStart hook injects everything the seat's last N SESSIONS wrote (timeline_inject config, log_event tail --sessions — the window is a sitting, not a row, so a session that logged more than once never shortens the recalled history) so a session starts sighted, not cold — live human-driven sessions only (headless spawns never inject; liveness read off the process ancestry since hooks run detached from the controlling terminal), seats resolved per-dir (each dir its own seat, tails include ancestor dirs, never siblings). SessionEnd hook (default 'selfwrite') resumes a disposable duplicate of the just-ended session (bin/dub-session) for one turn to write its OWN seat-tagged timeline entry via bin/log_event — the cheapest, best-informed writer — then deletes the duplicate, so the primary transcript never grows a self-write turn (clean future resume, clean picker); a resumed session that ends again gets the engine-computed last-reviewed boundary injected, scoping its entry to the delta since the resume point; a full multi-phase review remains available as the 'review' action and the manual /post-session-review command. Portable across machines via userConfig — no hardcoded paths. Scheduler: a deterministic daemon (python3 -m scheduler) firing one-time and recurring agent runs on RFC-5545 RRULE schedules — the piece that STARTS a session rather than reviewing or remembering one. Timeout counts from spawn, TTFT/stall watchdogs kill hung turns, the daemon owns child pgids so kills are authoritative, catch-up covers downtime, per-job concurrency policy plus a global cap, and a usage-limited run defers to just after the quoted reset instead of losing the day. One package on every machine: a host declares its timezone, spawn environment, and workspace resolution in config/scheduler.json and nothing host-specific lives in the code. Needs python-dateutil.

agent_root.title: Agent workspaces root
agent_root.description: Directory that contains your per-agent workspaces — each as {Name}/ with a CLAUDE.md. JStack resolves every agent path under here. Example: ~/Agents or /Users/you/Projects/Agents.

repo_root.title: Code repos root
repo_root.description: Directory under which /jstack:day-audit discovers the git repos to audit (scanned to depth 2). Leave empty to default to the parent of agent_root — the usual layout where code repos are siblings of the agent workspaces. Example: ~/Projects or /Users/you/Work.

agent_registry.title: Agent registry (agents.json)
agent_registry.description: Path to the agent registry that maps each agent to its workspace and the repos it owns ({agent: {workspace, repos: [...]}}). /jstack:day-audit reads it to dispatch each repo's regression audit under its owning agent (which loads that agent's domain context). Leave empty to default to {agent_root}/agents.json. Absent/unreadable → every repo gets a generic auditor.

followup_backend.title: Follow-up backend
followup_backend.description: How /jstack:save files a follow-up reminder. One of: none | todo | reminders | slack. 'todo' appends to the followup_target file; 'reminders' adds to the macOS Reminders list named in followup_target; 'slack' POSTs to the webhook in env var SLACK_FOLLOWUP_WEBHOOK. Default: none.

followup_target.title: Follow-up target
followup_target.description: Backend-specific target. For 'todo': a file path (default <agent_root>/followups.md). For 'reminders': the Reminders list name (default 'Follow-ups'). Ignored for 'slack' and 'none'.
